flags: Third-party vendor platform Nudge Security lists DeepAI as compliant with SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR Level 1. None of these certifications are documented on deepai.org's own website, privacy policy, terms of service, or any dedicated security or compliance page.

A Business Digital Index security assessment rated DeepAI 91/100 overall but flagged 'medium risk to be leaked' with issues including 25 SSL configuration problems, 16 phishing/malware concerns, 8 corporate credential breaches, and 17% of employees reusing breached passwords. This contrasts with claims of advanced security certifications.

The privacy policy provides basic security statements (general contractual safeguards for international transfers) with no mention of encryption, security architecture, or compliance frameworks. No dedicated trust center or security documentation page exists.
User data, including generated content and prompts, is used to train AI models by default. Opt-out is available via privacy choices. Generated images are also public by default on the free tier.

The company has approximately 20 employees and $2.2M revenue (2025), which is relevant to its ability to maintain enterprise-grade security and compliance programs, though it does take on custom enterprise projects.
Terms of service cap liability at the amount paid or $100 (whichever is greater), limiting recourse for data breaches or service failures.
No Data Processing Agreement or Business Associate Agreement is mentioned, limiting viability for regulated data (healthcare, financial).
Users retain ownership of generated content; generated AI images are free of copyright. This is favorable for users, though enterprise buyers should confirm terms for their specific use case.
